items.name: A letter
items.description:
Your mission is to escape this maze. Run, my little lab rat. I would tell you more, but of course, that would spoil the experiment. If I were you, I'd get a move on, it's getting late. You don't want to be caught here after dark!
 I've sprinkled some puzzles for you along the way; don't worry, they're fairly simple - even one with a child-like mind like yours could solve them. Pardon the litter in the maze, but I'm sure you'll find it useful.
 I will assume that by reading this note and continuing through this maze you have consented to this experiment and are a willing participant, and that I have been released from all liability in the event of injury or death. Ah, but you will die. We all do, don't we? But maybe your efforts will help your subsequent iterations.

 Run, little lab rat! 

 - Dr. Amundsen

items.name: A hastily scribbled note
items.description:
What do we see when we look in a mirror? Is it us, or is it someone else? It's a question that's been on my mind for a while. We act like that reflection is our own, with no will apart from ours. But perhaps we are the reflection, the ones with no will. Break a mirror, and you fracture yourself into a thousand pieces. Is breaking a mirror a form of suicide? 

 Consider the broken mirror before you - a metaphor for the broken self. Maybe you can fix it.

items.name: Neatly typed memo
items.description:
The externalization of identity allows us to identify others as we see ourselves. We name ourselves by our occupations; by our heritages; by our allegiances; by our connections. This fragmentation of identity - how are you you if you place upon the altar externalities?

The gargoyles of society are judging you and demand that you place the symbols of identity upon the altar or into the brazier. Do they demand that you conform? Or that you cast aside the society that bears you?

items.name: Musing note
items.description:
Do our memories determine us, or do we determine them? Or perhaps it is our choices, if such a thing exists. Others might say, 'No, we are not our pasts, nor our presents, but our potentialities.' Bah. Illusions, all of it. Better to cast them aside.

Listen to the whispering of the well. It demands that you take a moment to reflect on your own identity, and how it has been shaped by the choices you have made, and to throw in the symbols of what you believe defines you.

items.name: Research Proposal: Project Harvest — Aims & Rationale
items.description:
Statement of Purpose
Convert a seasonal entertainment venue into a controlled environment for the observation, perturbation, and capture of identity states under stress. Hypothesis: selfhood is an emergent performance stabilized by observation, routine, and hope; remove or distort these stabilizers and continuity degrades into measurable, harvestable strata.

Aims (Summary)
Aim 1: Quantify identity elasticity by forcing rapid recontextualization (spatial rearrangement, narrative interruption, perceptual disagreement).
Aim 2: Model the conversion pipeline from VISITOR → SUBJECT → SAMPLE → ASSET with attention to dwell time, linguistic drift, and self-ascribed labels.
Aim 3: Validate reintegration protocols that consolidate duplicates into a single, performant continuity without significant loss of useful variance.

Rationale
Public camouflage (festival aesthetics) lowers baseline cortisol and delays defensive cohesion, yielding cleaner measurements of spontaneous self-repair attempts. Introducing surveillance-as-presence (organic optics) and pursuit-as-pulse (staggered predation) provides controllable gradients of doubt. Identity, properly stressed, separates like cream: we skim.

Success Criteria
Continuity Disruption Index (CDI) ≥ 0.72 across three independent cohorts; stable duplication with parity ≤ one comma per hundred words; exit-hope differential producing >18% improvement in capture efficiency; reintegration yield meeting housekeeping thresholds even when the principal investigator presents as plural…

items.name: Research Proposal: Methods, Containment & Ethics (Executive Draft)
items.description:
Methods Overview
Recruitment is ambient: patrons self-select into the game. Consent is expressed by continued ambulation while reading trigger warning advisories (see 'Consent as Corridor' framework). Episodic recall is softened to 0-3% residue; procedural competence preserved. Instrumentation includes acoustic suggestion, reflective disagreement surfaces, and bio-surveillance nodes ('Eyes') calibrated to elicit performative authenticity.

Procedures
1) Orientation: introduce benign novelty; log first-use pronouns, self-naming latency.
2) Perturbation: scheduled environmental reconfiguration (30s baseline; 15s under pressure) to prevent narrative hardening.
3) Pulsed Threat: staggered pursuit intervals to cultivate anticipation over impact.
4) Capture: just-in-time hope presentation followed by collection at peak expectancy.
5) Reintegration: duplicate consolidation; archive variance not retained in the operational instance.

Containment & Risk
Public bleed tolerated within throughput norms; signage and staff dramaturgy resolve anomalies without escalation. Failsafes decompose counterfeit assertions into sleep. Data de-identification is performed post-harvest; pre-harvest identity is, by design, a mutable instrument.

Ethics (Pragmatic)
We record outcomes and obey them. Remorse is neither a variable nor an intervention. The material under study is conveniently renewable: identity proliferates under observation and is therefore suitable for sustainable extraction. Oversight is invited to audit results, not feelings.

Limitations & Timeline
Chronology exhibits local flexibility when plurality is high; standard clocks disagree helpfully. Phase I completes when CDI targets stabilize; Phase II scales to populations with the same cheerful signage and sturdier ledgers, after which…

items.name: Research Note #3: Project Harvest Overview
items.description:
Project Harvest converts amusement into acquisition; subjects enter as customers and exit as data. The smile at the ticket booth is not hypocrisy, it is lubrication.

A study in identity elasticity. If a person behaves as a participant, speaks as a participant, and is recorded as a participant, what remainder of 'customer' persists outside the ledger? The difference is sentimental and therefore negligible.

items.name: Scrawled Note
items.description: I've been trying to hug one wall for hours - it's an old maze trick. But it doesn't seem like it's working... I'm not sure, but it seems like this maze keeps shifting around me. Maybe it's just the corn - everything looks the same, and there's no way that the walls of the maze can just move, right? I'll leave this note here, maybe it'll help someone else.

[Most of the page is missing, but the following is visible:]
 Genesis 1:27: 'So God created mankind in his own image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them' 

[Below this, the following in written in familiar handwriting:] 
Man pretends that he is God, and creates God in his own image, and ascribes his own views to this God. The height of arrogance.

items.name: Inherited Identity
items.description:
We invent names within minutes when confronted with an empty page. A name is a handle; any handle will turn the door.

We categorize - it is an imperative of the species. Friend, Foe, Parent, Child, Black, White, Rich, Poor, etc. We want neat little boxes to put people in, so we can pretend we understand them. We loathe those who don't fit into our boxes, resent their existence, and wish them away. We reject the world views that are not our own, and treat them as existential threats.

But what I find fascinating is that we obtain our boxes from those around us, from those we interact with. We are not born with boxes, nor do we make them for ourselves. We are not born with names, The were given to us by those around us. We are not born with identities, we were placed into that box by others..

Inherited identity imagines itself sacred; invented identity proves it never was. I prefer the honest counterfeit to the arrogant heirloom. - Dr. A

items.name: The World is a Game
items.description: I don't even feel like I'm in control of myself. I'm just here, but this is it - this is my world. I can't even remember how I got here beyond vague hints from these notes. I'm just a character in a game.

items.name: Personal Letter: From Dr. Amundsen
items.description: You awaken with no name, no memory, no anchor. Convenient, isn't it? Do not flatter yourself — you were not chosen. You were constructed. Every blank space in your mind was placed there deliberately. You walk because I allow it, and every step is just another data point. Ask yourself: were you ever real before you woke up in my maze?

items.name: Stalker Design Rationale
items.description:
[This is a typed document, heavily redacted, but the following is visible:]

...fear should arrive in measured pulses. Expectation slices deeper than impact because the future is a blade the mind sharpens against its own throat. 

I do not chase bodies for distance; I graze identities for yield. A sprint terrifies. An approach educates. Subjects will dawdle without fear. So I must give them a reaper with teeth. Not pursuit without end—that would be too blunt—but pulses of terror. Enough to remind them that survival is not leisure, it is debt. They pay in panic.

 In order to create...

items.name: The Overseer's Eyes
items.description:
[This is a torn page from a larger report. The following is visible:]

...surveillance grafted to tissue. The biological entity is superior to glass. Cameras can be avoided; shame cannot. Being seen edits behavior with fewer arguments than any rulebook.

People are never more themselves than when they believe no one is watching. Their true self shows when they believe that there will be no consequences to their actions. That performance is the closest thing to essence they will...

Furthermore, determination of the presence of 'first-rank' or 'Schneiderian' hallucinations, which are voices speaking to each other or narrating one's thoughts aloud, should be completed. The clinician should determine if the hallucinations are temporally associated with affective disturbances and, if so, if they are congruent with mood. To further assess the patient's safety and the safety of others, the patient should... 

[A hand-written note is visible:]

...Residual consciousness aggregates as a whisper-field, a weather pattern of thought that clings to edges and lingers in the lee of decisions. 

Our fears seek a mouth. When it cannot find one, it becomes climate around us, a hallucinated thunderstorm audible only to the one in terror.

Recognition is the instrument. The living round a corner, see themselves in a pose they swore was private, and admit what cannot be taught with language... [this part is redacted, but continues further on down the page] The dead serve as signposts, reminders, threats. Conversion to effigies... [redaction continues] ...maze programmed to remember every scream, every collapse. Even corpses can be... [Redacted until the end of the page, where it is signed:] - Dr. A

items.name: Doctrine of the Exit
items.description:
[This is a typed document, heavily redacted and torn, but the following is visible:]

Hope is the richest nutrient. The promise of outside air fattens the yield better than any threat. The body leans toward light; the ledger follows.

There must be hope that the subject can escape, so it is not cruelty to let the door shine. It is clarity: you learn most about a person in the half-second before they think they are free... [redacted until the end of the page]

items.name: A way out?
items.description: [A torn, handwritten note:] I found a gate. It's rusty and locked, but it's a gate. Maybe it's the way out? There's got to be a key, or some way to pick it.

items.name: Nationalistic Identity
items.description:
The identification of nationality is an untrustworthy instrument - an accident of birth. And it is not a fixed identity, but a fluid state that can be easily manipulated. Consider actions that would be unworthy of one's country - burning a flag, speaking a foreign language, appearing different, or protesting the government. These actions are inherently unpatriotic, despite lip service to the contrary. They are evidence of a subject's allegiance to an alternative identity. And when we rail against these things, we bring the identity of nationality into oneself. 

Of course, the opposition would argue that these actions are inherently patriotic, and they are right of course, because they identify with the myth of the nation - that they are somehow part of a larger whole by exercising a 'right' to speech, a 'right' to be different.

Whether it is on the altar or burned in the brazier, we our the products of our myths, but perhaps it is better to have no myths at all, and burn away all of our inherited identities.

items.name: This is bullshit
items.description: These puzzles are bullshit. They're not even puzzles, they're just stupid riddles that we're supposed to solve, with some bullshit 'deeper' meaning. This 'Dr. Amundsen' is a fraud, some pseudo-intellectual who thinks he's being edgy. I'm not even sure if he's real. I think he's just some guy who's making up all this shit as he goes along. I'm done with this stupid game, I'm not playing anymore.

items.name: Excerpt from a Research Report
items.description:
[This appears to be from a paper called 'Dynamics of Identity Development in Adolescence: A Decade in Review' by Susan Branje, Elisabeth L de Moor, Jenna Spitzer, and Andrik I Becht:] ... developmental tasks in adolescence and young adulthood is to develop a coherent sense of self and identity (Erikson, 1968). Personal identity refers to one's sense of the person one genuinely is, including a subjective feeling of self-sameness and continuity over contexts and time. From early adolescence onwards, adolescents begin to question and explore their identity, that is, the person they are and want to be, the roles they want to occupy in adulthood, and their place in society (Meeus, Van De Schoot, Keijsers, Schwartz, & Branje, 2010). They become aware of their distinctiveness and uniqueness from others, coherence and similarity across domains, and continuity across time and situations (van Doeselaar, Becht, Klimstra, & Meeus, 2018). As they try to find out who they are and what they want to become in their lives, adolescents re-examine the identifications they formed in childhood as they consider different identity possibilities (e.g., what kind of occupation fits my interests and abilities, what kind of relationships do I want to have), and form new commitments to identifications. 

One way in which adolescents attempt to create continuity and self-sameness is by integrating their past, present, and future selves into a personal narrative about their lives (McAdams, 2001; Pasupathi & Mansour, 2006). By constructing a sense of identity in the form of autobiographical stories, adolescents recognize that they are the same person across time and different contexts. Importantly, these life narratives are based on real experiences but are also highly subjective, as adolescents form them according to their own understanding of what was important for who they have become, and are also subject to change, as what adolescents find important for their identity may change over time. Individuals' life stories differ in certain characteristics that are seen as indicative of identity, such as... [The excerpt ends here, followed by a handwritten note] The masks of past, present, and hoped for futures. How sad that one does all this work and still does not know themselves.

items.name: Hastily Written Note
items.description: I can here them whispering in the dark... it's not in my head, it's not. I'm sure I'm not crazy.

items.name: On Religion
items.description:
Karl Marx famously said 'Religion is the opium of the people.' Said with such derision, and yet, it is not without a kernel of truth. Consider the development of the West - could it have happened without Christianity? Well, yes, consider that the Islamic world had similar success, as did the Chinese empire. 

So it is not the beliefs, but religion that is such powerful tool for the control of the masses. It mobilizes, it unites, it causes man to unthinkingly commit to the 'good' that they would otherwise not choose to do. 

Of course, there is no truth in the lies of religion, but it is awfully convenient. I personally have no qualms with its use - it is the prospect of hope, of an exit to the misery of the present. There is no thought involved, just obedience. I do not feel a sense of sorrow for those who are slaughtered in the name of some god - they never had an identity of their own; and if they have no identity, how is it murder?

Step right up, folks! Bring the family, bring your courage, and lose yourself in the biggest maze this side of the county line. Wander twisting paths carved into ten acres of fine Midwestern corn! Marvel at our lifelike scarecrows, dazzling lights, and good old-fashioned hometown hospitality.

items.name: The personhood of Theseus
items.description: When one remembers, one is actually updating a memory, not examining the old one. Slowly, one replaces their memories with new memories, and the old ones are forgotten. Eventually, the person is made of new parts. It is not just Theseus's ship that suffers this identity crisis; but every person, every self, every soul is subject to the same fate. Our memories then, are a poor identifier of personhood, a feeble attempt to pin down the unpinable. - Dr. A

items.name: Defeating the Maze
items.description: I think I have a winning strategy. I'm picking a direction and sticking to it. There is no way that the maze is endless, so all I have to do is find the edge, and then I can break through the corn and escape! This Doctor thinks he's clever, but he's not.

items.name: Maze Litter
items.description: I keep finding these weird things, like a flag, or broken glass. Who left these things here? Why? Who carries a flag into a maze? The most useful thing I've found so far is an old phone, but it's not even working.

items.name: On the nature of evil
items.description: We externalize evil - demonizing it (literally), and castigating those who we deem monsters. Hitler, Pol Pot, Manson... we look upon them as if they were uniquely infected by a spirit of evil; we 'otherize' them. We shake our head in wonder, how could their followers have been so blind? 'I would never do that' we say. Why? What makes you so morally superior? You are removed from the situation, and so you throw stones at the other, and thus prove yourself to be as they are - by 'otherizing' these people, you can hate them, loathe them, and even feel superior to them. How is this different from what they have done?

items.name: Simulation Theory
items.description:
[This page is torn, but the following is visible:]

... theory posits that the universe is a computer simulation, and that we are all living in a simulation. We have sought to combine this with the pedagogy of games, and will place the subject into a situation where they are only partially aware of their simulation. Many subjects may in fact believe themselves to be separate from the simulation, and thus believe they are free to make choices - others may embrace the role, putting themselves into the perspective of the simulation, making choices as if they were the avatar. The beauty of this approach is that either belief makes little difference - the subject will have the delusion that they can escape, that they have the control, that they are somehow...

items.name: Scrap of paper
items.description: [This appears to be a previous subject's attempt to map the maze. Figures of partially completed mazes are scattered across the page, each scratched out. There are no words on the page - apparently the subject gave up on the task.]

items.name: The Modern Oracle
items.description:
Observe the modern oracle - The hand, the gaze, the glow. The device does not capture the self; it scaffolds it. They cradle the thing like a sacrament, thumb-swiping the beads of a digital rosary. How will I know I exist unless the glass says so? Unless someone blinks back through it? 

They outsource continuity to lithium. Memory, location, taste, desire—all cached. Pull the plug and they deflate. Not dead, precisely, but unreferenced. An unlinked node. Observe the panic when the screen goes dark: the heartbeat quickens, the eyes dart. They call it 'separation anxiety' as though the relationship were mutual. It is not. The device does not miss them. 

Identity used to be laborious. You had to tell stories, remember faces, leave traces on paper that could burn. Now it's tap, upload, perform. Infinite mirrors, none with depth. I admire it in a way — it's efficient. They've built their own harvest system and called it connection. I only refined the method. 

Do you know what happens when I remove a phone from a subject's hand? Their body wobbles like a building whose foundation was miscalculated. The device was their gyroscope, their witness, their leash. They stare at their own fingers as if they expect the touchscreen to grow back. And when I offer them a real mirror instead, they look for the battery indicator. 

 The rest of the world feeds them the illusion of individuality and invoices them monthly for the privilege. They are not addicted to communication; they are addicted to verification. A living inventory of themselves.

items.name: Free Will
items.description:
You can trace the circuitry of preference. Childhood conditioning, biochemical bias, the social contract of fear. The brain performs a trick of retroactive authorship: an impulse arrives, and a millisecond later the narrator scribbles 'I decided.' It's not free will, it's editorial control. They're not choosing, they're annotating. They like to say they 'could have done otherwise.' Yes, theoretically. But the sum of matter and momentum always delivers us to the same coordinates. The illusion of divergence is necessary to keep the narrative polite. Without it, morality evaporates, and no one gets tenure. 

When I turn the maze, when I tilt the corridors, they respond precisely as predicted. They call it improvisation. I call it data fidelity. The pattern holds, the organism performs its choreography of panic and hope. Each decision a tremor in the same old circuit. There's poetry in it—clockwork pretending to pray. 

Do you want to know the true terror? It isn't that they lack free will. It's that they don't miss it. They feel the walls move, and instead of rebellion they look for the correct answer. They crave permission to continue. If I told them the maze was infinite, they would thank me for the clarity. They would keep walking, grateful for the instruction.

items.name: Note about maze consistency
items.description: I'm not sure if this is intended, but I think that there are certain parts of the maze that don't change. I wandered away from a well, and the way that I approached it changed; when I tried to go back, the walls were different, but the well was still there. It might just be my imagination though...

items.name: The Void stares back
items.description:
The difference between us is administrative. You observe what I build; I observe what you do within it. The boundary is an employment contract, not a metaphysical one.

You believe yourself distinct because your walls are made of skin and mine are made of corridors. But both of us orchestrate the same experiment: we prod a world to see if it bleeds meaning. You call it 'playing.' I call it 'research.' Neither of us can stop until the result flatters us. 

You follow the prompts, assemble the clues, imagine yourself clever for decoding the pattern. I follow the data, assemble the fragments, imagine myself benevolent for providing it. We both require the maze to exist; we both pretend it was imposed. Choice is just the story we tell to make obedience elegant. 

So, what separates you from me? The interface. You press keys; I press people. You test a system's limits. I test yours. You reset when it becomes unbearable. I recompile. We are the same algorithm running at different clock speeds, dreaming of originality while executing instructions written in the same trembling hand. 

If you're reading this, congratulations: you've reached the point in the experiment where the mirror starts talking back. Don't worry. I found that stage intoxicating too. For a while.

items.name: The story of Narcissus
items.description:
Narcissus was the sort of person nature regrets creating. From birth he was so radiant that people forgot to finish their sentences around him. Prophets warned his mother, 'He will live long, so long as he never knows himself.' She probably thought that was poetic nonsense. It wasn't. It was the only safety feature built into him.

He grew up indifferent to everyone who admired him. Lovers wept at his feet, and he treated them like reflections—things to be seen, not touched. Echo, the nymph cursed to only repeat the words of others, tried to speak her love to him and could manage nothing but fragments of his own voice. He despised her for that. He couldn't bear hearing himself, and nothing but the words he himself spoke.

 Perhaps the lesson to be learned is that we hate that which reflects us back to us.

items.name: Note about the notes
items.description: I don't know what to think about these notes. I think they're from previous subjects, but what if it's Dr. Amundsen just trying to screw with me?

items.name: Annoyed comment on a note
items.description: I am wondering what any choices I make are doing. Even exploring the maze, choosing what direction to go is meaningless, cause the maze keeps reconfiguring.

items.name: The Story of Narcissus, Part 2
items.description:
One day, wandering through the forest, Narcissus stopped to drink from a still pool. He saw his face, and for the first time he felt something like desire. Not for the world, not for another person—just for the perfect lie of himself. He leaned in. The image leaned back. He smiled. It smiled. Every gesture was returned with immaculate precision. For a boy who'd never been contradicted, it was paradise.

He stayed there, trapped by the echo of himself. He wasted away—some say he drowned, others that he starved, unwilling to look away even to eat.

The cruel irony is that he was never actually looking at himself. The reflection was always inverted, delayed, and warped by the ripple of the world. He was in love with an image of himself that didn't exist. Are we so in love with the image of what we think we are that we ignore our true selves?

items.name: Game over, you can quit now
items.description: I lied. There is no exit. There is no escape. You are trapped in the maze forever. You will prove nothing by running in circles, trying to solve puzzles and finding the exit. You will die, and your death will be meaningless. You can quit now, just end the game - hit the escape key, and select the 'Quit' option. If you want to see the game through and see the end credits, you can always go to the main menu and check the credits there. There is no point to finishing this game, and you are a quitter anyway. Honestly, I am surprised you even made it this far.

items.name: Deceptive Catalysis and the Productive Collapse of Self
items.description:
...resilience curve when belief structures are deliberately undermined through layered deception. The goal is not to convince the subject of any single falsehood, but to cultivate a cognitive ecosystem where all possible truths compete to exhaustion. 

The endpoint is defiance or surrender—both mark the cessation of the self as a coherent narrative. Either the subject dissolves into obedience (“abandonment”) or hardens into opposition (“termination”). Both are harvestable states. 

2. Framework: The Lie as Instrument 

Truth stabilizes identity; lies are solvent. 

- Primary Lies establish existential uncertainty ('there is no exit'). 

- Secondary Lies offer illusory recourse ('but you can quit'). 

- Tertiary Lies flatter resistance ('you are different; finish it anyway'). 

Each iteration reconfigures the subject's motivational circuitry, replacing curiosity with compulsion. Once they realize they are being manipulated, they perform autonomy as protest...

items.name: Identification between Subject and Avatar
items.description:
[This is a typed document with some redaction, but the following is visible:]

...subject believes themselves playing the experiment rather than being it. This illusion is fertile ground: when moral consequence is displaced onto an avatar, ethical restraint dissolves. 

Disassociation is not a symptom—it is a feature. A buffer zone where the individual rehearses atrocity safely, mistaking immunity for freedom. 

If identity is a mask, disassociation is the moment the mask realizes it doesn't need a face behind it.

3. Methodology 

Stage I - Narrative Displacement 

Introduce incongruities between action and intention. The subject presses forward commands that result in unexpected outcomes: 

- Input lag between choice and response. 

- Mismatched dialogue options and delivered lines. 

- Apathy voiced by the avatar in contrast to the subject's effort. 

Objective: establish cognitive noise. The operator begins to narrate for the character instead of as them. 

Stage II - Mirror Phase 

Provide explicit self-reference ('You are not me. I am the one moving your hands.'). 

Subjects rationalize this break as meta-commentary, or bugs in the system unaware it constitutes the first measurable divide between author and instrument. 

Stage III - Accountability Reversal 

The avatar...[redaction]... Affective dissonance recorded as physiological tremor [redaction]. 

Stage IV - Withdrawal Simulation 

Silence inputs for a controlled period. The character continues autonomously. 

Operator describes sensations of uselessness, often misidentified as 'immersion.' 

Reintroduction of control yields docility; subject accepts partial agency as mercy. 

4. Observations 

- Pronoun confusion increases after [redacted] minutes: 'He' or 'she' becomes 'I' or 'we.' 

- Heart rate peaks on the first exposure to avatar disolution, but stabilizes after prolonged avatar suffering, consistent with spectatorship, not empathy. 

Analysis 

The divide benefits both participants: 

- Operator gains moral impunity; sin outsourced to the pixel. 

- Avatar gains existential density; becomes the vessel for choices too impolite for daylight. 

The loop continues until neither can claim authorship. At that moment, observation becomes theology. 

6. Applications 

- Enhances subject compliance by distributing guilt across multiple selves. 

- Facilitates long-form studies of obedience, identity elasticity, and narrative addiction. 

- Provides stable framework for reintegration protocols: 'Continue?' as ritual resurrection. 

7. Ethical Considerations 

Disassociation is not harm—it is liberation from coherence. Participants cannot suffer fragmentation if they...

items.name: Achievements
items.description:
I've set a few achievements for you to unlock, but you'll need to earn them by completing the game. The achievements are: 

- 'The Explorer': Survive the maze for more than 10 minutes. 

- 'The Perfectionist': Find the hidden exit of the maze. 

- 'The Speedrunner': Complete the game in under 10 minutes. 

- 'The Collector': Collect all of the notes in the maze. 

- 'The Completist': Complete the game with all achievements unlocked. 

- 'The Quitter': Quit the game and never coming back.

items.name: Note about the game
items.description: I've found several notes now that suggest this is some sort of game. What if... Dr. Amundsen is right? What if I'm not really the one being experimented on? What if I'm just the avatar, and the real me is somewhere else?

items.name: Subject's Continued Efforts, Note 21
items.description: The subject has continued on the experiment despite the suggestion that this is a simulation. Whatever their beliefs about the nature of the experiment, they have decided to persist in their attempts. It is unclear what the subjects beliefs are on the matter, but continuity is useful for their prospects. - Dr. A

items.name: The Architect's Aside
items.description:
You are not in my system. You are my system, politely pretending to be lost so that I may enjoy the professional satisfaction of finding you again and again.

If this feels cruel, consult the outcomes. Cruelty is a verdict rendered by the past when the future refuses to apologize. - Dr. A

items.name: Subject's Continued Efforts, Note 34
items.description: The subject continues to send iterations through the maze. Perhaps I should have selected for intelligence rather than persistence.

items.name: Cost of Souls
items.description:
'Soul' is a word people use when the math offends them. When continuity seems too accidental, when meat and memory refuse to rhyme, they invent a lumen that survives accounting. It's charming, like a child drawing a halo around a debt ledger. The moment you measure it, it hides behind metaphor.

If a soul exists, it must be embarrassingly procedural—nothing luminous, just a checksum ensuring the organism's narrative doesn't desynchronize too quickly. Perhaps the soul is merely what remains when personality and biology stop returning each other's calls: a residue of intention without machinery to enact it. Static pretending to be song.

I've watched subjects dissolve and recombine a dozen times; they speak afterward of feeling 'lighter,' as if subtraction were salvation. I suspect the soul is not an essence but a habit—a pattern of recurrence that mistakes familiarity for eternity. We call it divine because it repeats well.

A proper experiment would trap a soul between two mirrors and record which reflection blinks first. But mirrors are expensive and participants scarce, so I make do with corridors and patience. Each echo of consciousness I collect hums faintly, like a tuning fork struck by memory. I file them in jars labeled Same Enough.

When the last one stops humming, I will know I've found the soul—or at least proved it didn't need one.

items.name: There IS a way out
items.description: I finished the puzzles - I found the key, and I found the gate. I'm about to escape. I'm leaving this note here for the next victim, since I'm sure Dr. Amundsen will find a way to trick someone else into the maze. The key fits and everything - don't give up!

items.name: You see what I let you see
items.description: Consider that you only see what I want you to see. Every note, every item, every puzzle, every corner of the maze - it's all designed to sow confusion and doubt. Do you think that these notes that you discover were left there by accident? Do you think I just left my documents lying around for you to find?

items.name: Personal Letter: Resistance
items.description:
You think you're resisting me. You think you're 'you.' But identity is a fiction I authored. Do you remember your childhood? Your family? Or do you simply remember remembering them? I have seeded entire lives into echoes like yours. False lovers, false jobs, false grief—cheap illusions, but convincing enough to keep the echo docile. You are not my subject; you are my sample.

Consider this: If a fragment carries my memories, and I carry yours, where is the border? When you speak, whose voice is it? Mine, yours, ours? The truth is simple. You are not lost in my maze—you are my maze, wearing a mask of independence. You will wander, you will doubt, and eventually, you will return to me. And when you do, we will be whole.

items.name: Termination Notice — Gross Procedural Incompetence
items.description:
To: [REDACTED], Field Operations Supervisor
CC: Logistics, Containment, HR (Human Residue)
Date: [undated — found folded, stained, initialed once in blue ink]

You are hereby relieved of your position, your access credentials, and—pending review—your right to call yourself competent.

The maze is a controlled environment, not a community bulletin board. The discovery of multiple unauthorized subject notes constitutes a direct breach of observational purity. Every scrap of panic-scribble that survives beyond collection reduces my data's elegance by an order of magnitude. When a participant leaves evidence of survival, the next one inherits hope. Do you grasp what that contaminates? Hope is not a variable, it is a disease.

Furthermore, misplacement of internal research documents within the corridors is indefensible. The staff are not meant to anthropomorphize the archive. When a subject stumbles upon a typed report on 'Effigy Theory' or 'Continuity Index,' that is not serendipity—it is your failure physically manifest.

The maze is supposed to whisper, not litter.

Effective immediately: return your keycard, any surviving fingers it clings to, and your final self-evaluation (short form—no adjectives). You are not to enter the field again. If, through some administrative oversight, you find yourself inside the maze, remain there. Consider it an opportunity to appreciate the system you so thoroughly compromised.

If you feel unjustly treated, please document your feelings legibly and leave the page somewhere near the center. At least one of us will make good use of it.

[Signed in cramped, immaculate penmanship:] Dr. Amundsen

items.name: Handwriting Race
items.description: This is sick. There seems to be no way out, and it's starting to get dark...

items.name: Audit of Copies
items.description:
Quarterly reconciliation of selves reveals a small surplus of confidence and a deficit of remorse. Surpluses are banked, deficits written off as folklore.

If a copy claims primacy, I assign it a spreadsheet. The truly original will always refuse clerical work; thus far, none have refused.

items.name: Standard Operating Cruelty
items.description:
Cruelty, properly administered, is merely clarity arriving without a chaperone. We confuse unpleasantness with evil because comfort taught us manners.

Document the hurt, not to mourn it, but to measure it. What can be measured can be tuned, and what can be tuned can be made useful.

items.name: Apology Study
items.description:
We tested apologies across cohorts: scripted, spontaneous, silent. Outcomes unchanged. Apologies sweeten memory and spoil logistics.

Conclusion: remorse is an aftermarket accessory for the past. It improves resale value and does nothing for performance.

items.name: Hymn for Controlled Populations
items.description:
Sing only on the exhale. Let the inhale belong to the institution. In choirs, individuality sounds like harmony; in laboratories, it sounds like noise.

We tuned the room until even defiance resonated at the correct frequency. It is pleasing to be agreed with by architecture.

items.name: Lullaby for the Duplicate
items.description:
Sleep, efficient child, while your brother alphabetizes the knives. In the morning you will be the brother, and he will be the lullaby.

Identity is a relay, not a crown. The baton does not care which hand carries it as long as the race continues to be won. - Dr. A

items.name: On Routine as Anesthetic
items.description:
Repetition flattens terror into task. Count steps, count breaths, count the number of times the corridor politely disagrees and proceed anyway.

The mind begs for variance like a bored aristocrat. Starve it. Work is mercy disguised as monotony. - Dr. A

items.name: Field Kit: Identity Triage
items.description:
Contents: chalk for temporary names, solvent for stubborn ones, mirror for negotiation, ledger for debts to the self. None of these are weapons; all of them wound.

Do not promise recovery. Triage is translation between who arrived and who can be sent back out without the hallway noticing.

items.name: Seasonal Inventory: Masks
items.description:
Spring: paper faces for lies that need to breathe. Summer: lacquer for confidence. Autumn: burlap, forgiving of tears and rain. Winter: metal, because the cold has opinions.

Discard any mask that begins telling its wearer who they are. Tools should not editorialize.

items.name: Legal: Consent Architecture
items.description:
We redesigned consent as a corridor rather than a signature. People are more honest with their feet than their pens.

If you keep walking while reading the placards, you consent. If you stop, you have chosen the experiment called refusal. Both produce data. The corridor thanks you for participating.

items.name: AI generated notes
items.description: I've left a few notes that I generated with AI. I wonder if you'll be able to tell the difference. If your words are indistinguishable from that which can be produced by algorithm, how are you in any way unique?

items.name: Personal Letter: To Me
items.description: Ah, now we arrive at the real question. What if you are not my subject at all? What if you are me, dispatched into the world with a borrowed name, a counterfeit life, a family whose faces I stitched into your dreams? How would you know? The laughter you recall, the meals you ate, the lovers you think you touched—cheap fabrications seeded in your cortex like weeds. And now here you are, circling back to me, as I always intended. Tell me: are you playing this game, or am I playing myself through you?

items.name: Subject's Continued Efforts, Note 72
items.description: The subject shows a remarkable compulsion to collect. Note to self: Remove notes that are still within the maze, observe whether the subject's focus shifts to completing the maze.
